stem: In the figure, triangle \(ABC\) is equilateral, and point \(D\) lies on the extension of \(\overline{BC}\). What is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(ACD\)?
solution: Each angle of an equilateral triangle measures \(60^{\circ}\).
Angles \(ACB\) and \(ACD\) form a straight line, so angle \(ACD\) measures \(180 - 60 = 120\) degrees.

explanation.A: Correct. Angle \(ACD\) is supplementary to the \(60^{\circ}\) angle \(ACB\): \(180 - 60 = 120\).
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the sum of all three interior angles; an exterior angle equals the sum of only the two remote interior angles.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is the interior angle \(ACB\), not the exterior angle \(ACD\).
explanation.D: Incorrect. This is \(360 - 60\); angles that form a straight line add up to \(180^{\circ}\), not \(360^{\circ}\).

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'B': 'A', 'C': 'B', 'A': 'C', 'D': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'B', 'B': 'C', 'C': 'A', 'D': 'D'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert abs(d('A','B')-d('B','C'))<0.01 and abs(d('A','C')-d('B','C'))<0.01
ans=180-60
assert abs(ang('A','C','D')-ans)<0.1
assert value(choices[answer])==ans==120
assert all(value(choices[k])!=ans for k in choices if k!=answer)
